findings.reason: the worker would break every local follower registration the section says it preserves, and would need the plan to say how the lock survives the rewrite or to scope the rename to foreign registrations only.
findings.text: §8 sets the renewal write to replace the registration by rename, but the follower holds `flock(LOCK_EX)` on the registration inode (reckon/crew/follower_registration.py:293) and `_write_watch_record` writes in place precisely to keep that inode (reckon/crew/run_paths.py:50, "without replacing the inode carrying its lock"); a rename unlinks that inode, so a same-node reader's `flock` in `_follower_liveness` succeeds and the local registration reads `registered: False` — gone — contradicting the section's own guarantee that a same-host registration keeps its lock

findings.reason: the plan must serialize §9 against §13 (and §8/§12 against §13 on crew_follow_commands.py) or the nodes collide on the same functions and one change is merged blind.
findings.text: §9's write paths are `reckon/crew/watch_unit.py`, `reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py` and `reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py`, and §13's are `reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py`, `reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py` and `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py`; §8 and §12 also write `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py`, and neither a gate nor a followup orders any pair, so two nodes editing `not_fresh_line` and `freshness` at once — the exact functions §9 and §13 both change — are declared independent by omission

findings.reason: the parse test guards the very count the exit-status change acts on and both sit on one surface, so splitting earns little and the author may reasonably decline.
findings.text: §12's title and deliverable join two tasks §5's own review listed separately ("first, the command still exits 0 … second, `restart_count` … no test pins that parse"): the `--ensure` exit-status change and a new parse test, so one verdict must close two deliverables

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — §8's `_write_watch_record` (reckon/crew/run_paths.py:50), `renew_producer_lease` (reckon/crew/runs.py:1764), `producer_lease_seconds` (runs.py:1702) and `_follower_liveness` (reckon/crew/follower_registration.py:482); §11's `resume_plan` (reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1008) with its mirror guard (reckon/crew/resumption.py:820) and `launch_in_flight` (resumption.py:179); §12's `restart_count` (reckon/service.py:347); §13's `reload_in_progress` (reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:445) and `not_fresh_line` (reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:729); §10/§11's `_newest_stream_in_motion` (reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:194) all resolve, and the cited evidence archive docs/evidence/archive/a-seat-held-elsewhere-is-not-restarted-landed.html exists.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each changed node declares a negative control that can fail: §8 restores the lock judgement so the fresh-renewal case reads gone, §11 removes the exclusive claim so both resume doors launch, §12 leaves the exit status at 0 so the cycling case reads healthy, §13 restores the direct `not_fresh_line` print so the stop line shows `--ensure`.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §8, §11, §12 and §13 log their negative controls "under the run directory", a durable path under the shared crew home, not a node-local scratch directory or a session scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the changed sections introduce no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags; new symbols are named by mechanism (`_newest_stream_in_motion`, `cycling`, `reload_in_progress`) and the test files by behaviour.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §8 states "A registration from this host keeps its lock and pid probes" while its own mechanism, a renewing write that "replaces the file atomically, with a temporary file and a rename", replaces the inode the follower holds its exclusive lock on, so a same-node reader opens an unlocked file and reads the local registration gone.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §12 carries two deliverables (make `--ensure` exit non-zero on a cycling unit, and add a parse test for `SystemdUserUnitManager.restart_count`), the two §5 follow-ons merged into one node.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §9 and §13 both write `reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py` and `reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py`, and §8, §12 and §13 all write `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py`, but no gate or followup orders them, so dispatched together they collide on the same functions.
